title: What Happens When Sales Promises an Urgent Order
description:
When sales promises an urgent delivery date, the order lands in a factory schedule that is already full, and other customers quietly absorb the delay. This episode is for manufacturing planners, operations leaders and data architects who connect ERP, MES and analytics. It shows how to turn urgent requests into visible, tested trade-offs with a shared promise process and a layered decision architecture.
In this episode
00:00 – The urgent order and the factory scenario05:45 – A promise is not a production plan10:10 – Machine time, displaced orders, material and labor34:00 – Shifting bottlenecks, OEE and cascading delivery dates52:50 – Excel, missing context and Microsoft Fabric as the data layer70:30 – Simulation, prediction and optimization79:05 – Who defines priority: governance and a shared promise process88:10 – Decision architecture, Copilot and human judgment
Key takeaways
A priority flag in ERP does not create capacity: an urgent order always takes machine time, material, people or inspection slots from existing commitments.Finite capacity scheduling and simulation make the trade-off visible before the plant moves, while OEE dashboards and Excel recovery files only describe parts of the situation.Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Power Platform and Copilot can connect ERP and MES facts and route approvals, but the feasibility decision needs scheduling logic, defined urgency categories and an accountable human owner.
